lines.text: Opus 5.5 draws first blood on the scoreboard. 1–0 inside six turns!
Player5 brings the second flag home and edges ahead, 2–1.
Four captures in eighteen turns. Neither side is wasting time on defence; they're just racing each other to the flags.
Player5 cuts down the Opus carrier and scores on the same turn. 3–2!
Back to back! 5–2 Player5, and this is turning into a statement.

First 50 turns: Player5 converted all 5 of its pickups, Opus only 2 of 5. Two carrier stops at turns 29 and 32 are the whole difference, and Opus pushing deeper, 8.5 cells from home against 5.0, left its carriers exposed.
Opus 5.5 finally gets one back. 5–3.
And another! Opus pulls within one, 5–4.
Player5 restores the two-point gap, 6–4.
Opus 5.5 again. 6–5 and it simply won't go away.
Player5 strikes back, 7–5.
Opus makes it 7–6, and Player5 answers a turn later. 8–6!

Turns 51–100 were even on paper, 4 captures to 3 for Opus, but the shape flipped: Player5 now sits 8.0 cells from home on average while Opus pulled back to 4.5. Opus is camping the flags; Player5 is escorting carriers in.
Player5 answers, 9–7.
Two in three turns! 11–7, the biggest lead of the match.
That double at turns 118 and 120 is the first real crack. Opus had matched everything until now, and suddenly it's four points adrift.
Opus stops the bleeding. 12–8.
Player5 straight back, 13–8.

Player5 scored 5 of the 8 captures in turns 101–150, all from clean escorts: it lost no carriers in that stretch. Opus has the kills to compete, but kills away from the carrier don't change the scoreboard.
Opus stopped a Player5 carrier on turn 154 and now turns it into a point. 13–10.
Opus scores, 14–11.
Opus has started hunting carriers instead of racing them. It's the right idea; it just needs a few more of them.
Player5 makes it 16–11.
Opus answers, 16–12.
Opus stops a Player5 carrier!

Halftime, 16–12 Player5. But the last ten turns matter more than the score: Opus had 3 kills and 2 carrier stops with no losses, and all three Player5 units are down at turn 200. The second half starts with Opus holding the middle.
Opus again! 16–14, the gap is two.
Three straight for Opus 5.5! 16–15.
Opus levelled at 16 on turn 222, but Player5 goes straight back in front, 17–16.
Opus scored four unanswered from 12 to 16. That's the momentum swing we've been waiting for all match.
Opus stops one carrier, but Player5 scores anyway. 18–16.
Opus 5.5 answers, 18–17.
Turns 201–250 went 5–3 to Opus. The key change is defensive: Opus now sits 6.0 cells from home and Player5 only 4.5. Player5 has been pushed back toward its own base for the first time.
Opus pulls one back, 19–18.
Opus levels at 19!
And Opus 5.5 leads for the first time since turn 6! 20–19!
From 12–7 down to 21–19 up. That's what happens when one team stops winning the fights and the other never stops believing.
Player5 finally answers, 22–20.
24–20 Opus 5.5. A four-point lead!
Turns 251–300: Opus 7 captures, Player5 1. Player5 is stuck 3.0 cells from home on average, defending its base instead of contesting the flags, and you can't score from there.
Player5 stops the Opus carrier!
Player5 scores, 24–22.
Player5 levels it! 24–24! Four straight!
Opus answers, back in front 25–24.
Player5 replies, 26–25.
Turns 301–350 went 5–3 to Player5, and the shape flipped again: Player5 is back out at 5.0 cells from home while Opus has retreated to 3.5. Whoever controls the middle in the final fifty decides it.
Level again! 27–27!
Player5 retakes the lead, 28–27!
Opus levels, 28–28!
Player5 in front again, 29–28!
Player5 makes it 30–28. A two-point cushion with fourteen to play!
Player5 scores with three turns left! 31–29, and that's the match!
